chapter_theme: A single song at Thiriyambakapuram (த்ரியம்பகபுரம்): courtesans who befriend men to seize their wealth, and the plea to be freed from that base work; the praise is a battle of drum syllables and ghosts drinking blood, and the gods bowing at the feet saying 'Kanda, given by Gauri'.

825.reading: The poet describes the women who see that men struck speechless are easy prey, befriend one and seize all his wealth, skilled in every art, the price-women whose breasts thrill and who make love in every way on the flower bed; they take what a man has earned and think others' wealth their own, and he asks to be freed from the base work of standing in their anger. The praise has Murugan mount the peacock to end the Asuras' age and free the world from fear, the drums sounding in syllables, ghosts drinking blood from a shoreless sea of it, the hunter girl embraced, and the gods bowing at Thiriyambakapuram saying 'Kanda, six-faced, given by Gauri'.
825.nuance: விலைமகள் is named outright. அயல் தனங்களும் தனது என நினைபவர்: the courtesans think others' wealth their own. வெகுளியின்கண் நின்று இழிதொழில் is obscure; it may mean the base life of serving their tempers.
